description: Dependency DAG of the Proximity Prize program. Nodes = statements/artifacts/experiments; edges point FROM a dependency TO the statement it supports. gate=all: every 'req' child needed; gate=any: one 'alt' child suffices (plus all 'req'). Statuses: PROVED (on main w/ proof or exact verification), PROVABLE (route pinned, write-up pending), CONDITIONAL (proved under stated hypothesis), CONJECTURE (precise statement, unproved), TARGET (fuzzy, expected to sharpen), WALL (frozen hard core w/ consumer theorem), REFUTED (dead route), TEST (experiment/prediction). Source of truth for statuses: experimental/notes/roadmaps/ (r2 + proof_sketch + wp_detail). REFINEMENT PRINCIPLES (2026-07-02): (1) critical nodes carry exact 'statement' fields (+ attack_surface/falsifier notes) — machine-enforced; (2) new conjectured nodes are admitted ONLY as branches of exhaustive splits, proved equivalences/reductions, or with a named non-ev consumer + truth-confidence note — never as speculative lemma chains presuming a proof shape; (3) every critical conjecture gets a cheap wired falsifier TEST. INTEGRATED UPSTREAM 2026-07-02 (commit 01add412, PR #174 closed-integrated): this DAG is in-tree subordinate roadmap material; towards-prize.md is the source of truth.

nodes.statement: For a prime-field row C=RS[F_p,D,k] with p congruent to 1 modulo n, quotient order N' dividing n, ell'=rho N'+1, and p>(2ell')^(N'/2), the canonical quotient line at radius 1-rho-1/N' has exactly Acl(N',ell') distinct quotient-value slopes. No below-threshold or extension-field conclusion is asserted.

nodes.title: Qfloor norm threshold is impossible at the six clean predecessors
nodes.statement: At the six clean candidate predecessors, the canonical qfloor parameters are (N',ell')=(256,65),(256,33),(512,33). Their strict norm thresholds (2ell')^(N'/2) have respectively 899, 774, and 1548 bits, all above 2^256. Since every official characteristic satisfies p<=q<2^256, qfloor_exact is inapplicable on all six rows. The above-budget raw binomial quotient censuses are not thereby proved to be distinct ambient slopes.

nodes.title: Exact E1 class counts and collision-loss allowances at clean anchors
nodes.statement: At each clean candidate predecessor, let K=A_2(N,ell) be the exact characteristic-zero antipodal-rearrangement class count and P=sum_y binom(r_y,2) the number of unordered pairs of distinct classes colliding after reduction into the ambient slope field. Then K-|image|<=P, so P <= K-B*-1 implies |image|>=B*+1. The actual quotient orders are N=256,512 with folded dimensions h=128,256. If B=F_p(Q) has size b, image(e1) is contained in B; moreover every reduction has P>=P_min(K,b)=b binom(s,2)+rs for K=sb+r. Thus b<=B* rules out direct E1, and b<b_pair_min=ceil((K+B*+1)/3) rules out the pair-loss compiler. Exact allowances and pair-feasibility thresholds are printed for all six anchors.
nodes.notes: FINITE E1 COMPILER 2026-07-26: corrects the provisional global-sign factor, quotient-order/folded-dimension ambiguity, circular route assignment, and the overbroad |B|>B* pair target. It fixes exact allowances and a three-way generated-field split but proves no official collision bound and pays no row.

nodes.title: Pair-feasible E1 rows generate the ambient field
nodes.statement: At each of the six named clean predecessor anchors, let Q be the canonical cyclic quotient root set of order N in {256,512}, and let B=F_p(Q) be its generated subfield of the ambient field F_q. Every proper B has |B|<2^128 because q<2^256. All six exact pair-feasibility thresholds satisfy b_pair_min>2^128, with bit lengths 134,170,188. Hence |B|>=b_pair_min forces F_p(Q)=F_q. Proper generated-subfield rows remain outside the pair-loss target and require direct image or another supplier.
nodes.notes: ROUTE REDUCTION 2026-07-27: ambient generation is automatic on the live pair-feasible E1 branch; this proves no collision bound.

nodes.title: Pair-feasible E1 rows lie in the prime-field kernel scope
nodes.statement: At each of the six named clean predecessor anchors, pair feasibility first forces F_p(Q)=F_q. Writing q=p^d, the canonical quotient roots then give d=ord_N(p), where N is 256 or 512. Exact perfect-power interval checks exclude every possible d>1: the prize interval has no such perfect power, and the only four RowC square roots have the wrong parity or multiplicative order. Hence q=p and p=1 mod N on the live pair-feasible E1 branch. This validates the prime-field sparse-kernel interface but proves no collision allowance.
nodes.notes: ROUTE REDUCTION 2026-07-27: closes the extension-degree scope gap left by ambient generation. The exact pointwise E1 collision target remains open.

nodes.title: Prime-field E1 collision-free radius from folded L2 norms
nodes.statement: For a nonzero E1 class difference with raw representatives at swap distance s over quotient order N=2h, fold antipodes to alpha=sum_i c_i zeta^i and S=sum_i c_i^2. Odd-conjugate orthogonality and AM-GM give |Norm(alpha)|<=S^(h/2). Either S<=4s-2, or alpha=2 beta with |Norm(beta)|<=s^(h/2). Since every live pair-feasible prime is at least 2^250, all N=256 collisions with s<=4 and all N=512 collisions with s=1 are impossible. The first surviving bands reduce to profiles (a,b,c)=(4,2,0),(3,4,0) at N=256,s=5 and (1,2,0),(0,4,0) at N=512,s=2.

nodes.title: E1 class-difference square-mass coordinates and finite height
nodes.statement: For signed singleton vectors x,y representing two antipodal-rearrangement classes, alpha=sum_i(x_i-y_i)zeta^i has square mass S=4a+b and height H=2a+b. If T=min(ell,2h-ell), then H<=2T and even S<=4T. Raw same-sign antipodal-pair padding changes representative distance but not alpha. At the official parameters S<=260 for N=256,ell=65 and S<=132 for ell=33. Every S=16 split with b>0, namely (3,4),(2,8),(1,12),(0,16), is realized by official-size N=256 class pairs and survives the present norm floor; the existing variance descent covers only (3,4). This reparametrization closes no collision ledger or prize row.

With N' = n/sigma, n_1 = N'/2, l' = rho N' + 1, let A(N',l') = sum over u >= 0, t = l' - 2u >= 0, u <= n_1 - t of binom(n_1,t) 2^t be the number of antipodal-rearrangement classes of l'-subsets of mu_{N'} (class invariant: the signed set of singleton antipodal pairs together with the number of full pairs). Then for every prime IN THE STABLE RANGE the canonical line's bad-slope count is exactly B(p) = A(N',l'), and at rho = 1/2, B(p) = (3^{n/(2 sigma)} - 1)/2. Consequently at safe slack B(p) = n^{beta(rho)/c_eff + o(1)} with beta(rho) = (1/2) max over 0 <= theta <= 2 min(rho,1-rho) of (H(theta) + theta). SCOPE FENCE (load-bearing): exactness holds only ABOVE THE QUOTIENT NORM THRESHOLD p > (2 l')^{N'/2}. At log2 q = 256 and rho = 1/2 that means N' <= 80 — zone (a) of proof_sketch/s2_paid_ledger.md#3, which is the PROVED-exact zone. The range 80 < N' < ~512 is zone (b), explicitly CONJECTURAL in that source and carried by the separate node `zone_b` (CONDITIONAL). This node claims only the zone-(a) exact count. nodes.statement: [transcribed 2026-07-27 from the upstream source read via git -C ../rs-mca show origin/main:experimental/notes/roadmaps/proof_sketch/prize_proof_sketch_spine.md#2, 'The exact counting frame (what is already rigorous)']. THE EXACT COUNTING FRAME. Fix a pair (u,v) and exact agreement A (t = A-k, j = n-A). Locators of co-supports are squarefree degree-j divisors of X^n - 1 — a FINITE set of size C(n,j), i.e. points in P^j coefficient space. The Hankel pencil is LINEAR in the slope: M(Z) l = a + Z b with a = H_{t,j}(u) l and b = H_{t,j}(v) l in F^t. Hence per valid locator l, when b != 0 there is at most ONE bad slope Z = -a_r/b_r (subject to the consistency condition) — the Paper D v12 quotient-support ledger's 'one support pays for at most one slope'.

nodes.statement: FM1 — THE FIRST-MOMENT ALIGNMENT COUNT (exact). Fix a support R of size j and write S = H \ R; the RS restriction to S has dimension k with |S| = k + t, so the quotient syndrome space has dimension t. For a received pair (u,v) with syndromes U,V in F^t of u|_S, v|_S, the support R is aligned at a finite slope z exactly when U + z V = 0 with V != 0 (the excluded V = 0 case is the standard all-slope/paid-fiber degeneracy and is not counted in this column). Counting q^t - 1 nonzero V and q choices U = -z V gives alignment probability q(q^t - 1)/q^(2t) = (1 - q^(-t)) q^(1-t), so by linearity of expectation over the binom(n,j) supports: E[#aligned] = binom(n,j) (1 - q^(-t)) q^(1-t). [statement written 2026-07-27 from this node's own proof.md]

nodes.statement: SUBGROUP HANKELS ARE FOURIER OBJECTS [transcribed 2026-07-27 from proof_sketch/s3b_iii_2_displacement_spectral.md#1, tagged 'elementary, verified'; upstream experimental/notes/roadmaps/]. For u supported on the subgroup H = mu_n with syndrome s_u[m] = sum_{x in H} u(x) x^m, the Hankel factors as H_{t,j}(u) = V_t^T D_u V_{j+1}, where D_u = diag(u(x))_{x in H} and V_m[x,r] = x^r (r < m). Consequently, for a locator l with root set (co-support) T and w_Z = u + Z v: M(Z) l = 0 IFF the function w_Z * l on H has vanishing Fourier coefficients at frequencies 0..t-1. Verified entrywise on the F_13 / mu_12 toy. A constant syndrome-indexing offset x^{c_0} absorbs into D_u (cosmetic). nodes.statement:
[lifted verbatim 2026-07-27 from this node's own proof.md Statement section] GAP-2 seam. In the normal-form / residue framework (`thm:normalform`,
`def:residue`, banked), a bad-slope datum on a residue line carries a
**denominator polynomial** `E in F[X]` of degree `t_denom` with
`1 <= t_denom <= r`, where `r = n - k`. Say the datum is a **pullback** if
`E = g(X^M)` for some `g in F[X]` and integer `M >= 2`. Claim:

1. **(Divisibility.)** A pullback denominator forces `M | t_denom`.
2. **(Strip coincidence.)** If moreover `M | gcd(n,k)`, then the line-side
   aperiodic strip (`rem:aper`: remove pullback denominators) coincides with
   the support-side **rate-preserving** quotient strip (the `Q_M = Q_1(H_{n/M})`
   recursion, banked): on every exact-agreement bucket `A`,
   `M | j  <=>  M | t_win`, where `j = n - A`, `t_win = A - k`.
3. **(Residual seam classified.)** The only strata that are periodic on the
   support side but *not* pulled back rate-preservingly are those with
   `M | gcd(n,j)` but `M !| k`: these are **non-rate-preserving folds** — the
   quotient row `(n/M, k/M)` is not integral, the syndrome conditions do not
   descend to a valid RS row, so they stay on the aperiodic side and carry no
   alignment boost (checker convention `rem:aper`).

Parts 1–2 are the load-bearing divisibility content and are proved here in full.
Part 3's classification is proved; its "no boost" clause is the banked
`rem:aper` convention, cited (not re-derived), and flagged as such.

nodes.title: B-rational pencils give B-slopes (linearity)
nodes.statement: [transcribed 2026-07-27 from the upstream source read via git -C ../rs-mca show origin/main:experimental/notes/roadmaps/proof_sketch/s6_extension_lift.md#1, tagged 'elementary']. THE TRIVIAL HALF OF THE EXTENSION LIFT. Let B = F_p(D) be the generated field and F contains B the ambient/sampling field. The alignment pencil is linear with coefficients a(l), b(l) built from the pair's syndromes; hence if the PAIR (and therefore its syndromes) is B-rational, every aligned slope Z = -a_r/b_r lies in B automatically. Consequently B-rational data cannot produce genuinely F-valued bad slopes: those require either F-valued words or the pole mechanism. This is the precise sense in which the lift is 'free' on generating rows, and the reason the safe-side classification is a Galois-descent question about the pencil data. SCOPE: that classification (same file, section 4) is CONJECTURE and is NOT claimed here.

nodes.statement: EXTENSION-POLE FLOOR [transcribed 2026-07-27 from proof_sketch/s6_extension_lift.md#2, tagged 'verified']. Paper D v12's extension-pole floor converts a base list of size L into genuinely F-valued witness lines with numerator N(L) = ceil( L(|F|-|B|) / (|F|-|B|+kL) ). Verified behaviour: N(L) ~ L below the saturation cap X/k ~ 2^216 (X = |F|-|B|, k = 2^40), essentially independent of |B|; the gate crossing N > |F|*2^-128 = 2^128 occurs exactly when the BASE list crosses L ~ 2^128. Hence B_ext crosses the MCA gate precisely at the list-side crossing window of S7 — the channel through which grand challenge 2's threshold enters grand challenge 1's ledger. SCOPE: the safe-side classification (same file, section 4) is CONJECTURE and is NOT claimed here.

nodes.title: Non-generating rows forced tiny (q_gen < 2^128)
nodes.statement: GENERATING ROWS ESCAPE THE POLE MECHANISM [transcribed 2026-07-27 from proof_sketch/s6_extension_lift.md#3, tagged 'verified']. The pole mechanism requires F \ B nonempty, i.e. a NON-generating row (q_gen < q_line). Admissibility forces such rows to be tiny at the base: q_line = q_gen^m with m >= 2 and q_line < 2^256 give q_gen < 2^128, hence base gate B*_gen = floor(q_gen/2^128) <= 1 and base reserve tau*(rho,q_gen) >= H(rho)/128. For PRIME fields the question vanishes (no proper subfields); for extension rows the minimal field containing mu_n is F_p^ord, and the pinned row is exactly the generating case (ord(17 mod 512) = 32). Therefore: generating rows (q_gen = q_line) leave B_ext degenerate and the S2 corridor stands; non-generating rows are bound by the imported S7 window.

nodes.statement: THE COMMON CODE-LINE RESIDUAL BUDGET (upstream experimental/notes/m2/m2_common_code_line_residual_budget.md, 'PROVED finite theorem for MDS codes'; the verifier there is marked EXPERIMENTAL). Let C <= F^D be MDS of dimension k (so a nonzero codeword has fewer than k zeros on D), |D| = n, a an agreement threshold, and fix a received line ell_z = f + z g. Assume codewords c_f, c_g in C and a common support S0 subset D of size b with f = c_f and g = c_g on S0, and a + b - n >= k. Put Omega = D \ S0, f' = f - c_f, g' = g - c_g, h = max(1, a-b), and c0 = |{x in Omega : f'(x) = g'(x) = 0}|. Then every support-wise noncontained slope at agreement a satisfies |{x in Omega : f'(x) + z g'(x) = 0}| >= h; consequently if h > c0 then #{support-wise noncontained slopes} <= floor((|Omega| - c0)/(h - c0)). This is the support-wise replacement for the ordinary 'the received line is close to a code-line' statement: residual noncontained slopes must be paid by residual zeros OUTSIDE the common support. (`n = 2^41`), together with the structural facts that make the profile
well-defined and computable: **first-scale dominance** and **n-uniformity**.

nodes.statement: Fix one maximal source and consider genuine degree-ell common-pencil recharts whose quotient partition carries one whole fixed-source petal. For every partition, include points outside its complete ell-fibers in the layout and defect polarities. Under fixed caps R_0,B_0,P_0, arbitrary partial source cores, complete-fiber source petals, every degree strip, ell>=c_0 n/log_2 n, ell>2P_0, and q<=n^gamma, the total across all anchored partitions and canonical charts is at most M_src(R_0+1)(B_0+1)(P_0+1)16^(n/ell)n^(R_0+B_0+P_0)q^(2P_0), hence polynomial. The strict-window and thin-edge CRT bounds pay all numerator/Forney multiplicity in this scope. Growing triple polarity, unanchored or smaller-fiber quotient maps, and arbitrary petal locators remain open.

nodes.title: L1 tame fixed-petal refinement census
nodes.statement: Fix one maximal source with M_src disjoint ell-point petals. For s|ell, put r=ell/s. If a monic degree-s quotient polynomial partitions one whole source petal into complete s-point level fibers, then its locator is F(P), with F monic split squarefree of degree r. When the field characteristic does not divide r, the top s-1 coefficients of F(P) recursively determine every nonconstant lower coefficient of P; its constant is exactly additive-shift freedom. Hence each petal carries at most one degree-s refinement class and all tame classes number at most M_src tau(ell)<=n. This counts maps only: small-scale fiber-role payment, wild divisors, unanchored maps, growing polarity, and arbitrary locators remain open. The exact F_9 decomposition of X^9-X into four inequivalent normalized cubic right components proves the tame guard cannot be removed by coefficient triangularity alone, but is not asserted to be an admissible-domain counterexample.

nodes.title: L1 tame-refinement periodic-owner obstruction
nodes.statement: On H=F_17^* with n=16, k=8, sigma=5, ell=6, the petal T={1,2,3,11,12,13} is the union of three complete fibers of the tame degree-two map P=X^2+3X. Taking core C={7,8,9,10,14,15,16}, remainder R={4,5,6}, and U zero on A=C union T and one on R, the zero codeword has exact agreement set A of size k+sigma. Yet Stab_H(A)=Stab_H(R)={1}. Thus a tame fixed-petal polynomial refinement does not force exact multiplicative periodicity or intrinsic cyclic quotient descent. The small-scale branch needs a general polynomial-pullback owner or collective aperiodic-support payment. This toy is a route fence, not an official-row L1 counterexample.

nodes.title: L1 general polynomial-pullback interleaving descent
nodes.statement: For every monic degree-s polynomial P, each degree-below-k polynomial has a unique normal form f=sum_(j<s)X^j g_j(P), with exact residue-dependent caps k_j=ceil((k-j)/s). On every complete s-point P-fiber, Vandermonde inversion turns agreement with an arbitrary received word into common agreement of the quotient tuple (g_j) with an s-component receiver on the fiber label. For b complete labels the quotient evaluation kernel has exact dimension kappa=sum_j max(0,k_j-b), so the contributor count is at most q^kappa times the common-support interleaved list for degree-below-ceil(k/s) evaluation on those labels. The proved interleaving collapse reduces this to q^kappa floor(L(q-1)/(q-L)), and to q^kappa L when L^2<q. A full complete-fiber domain partition with k<n has kappa=0. Partial fibers, sparse coverage, and ordinary list bounds on generally non-smooth label domains remain open.

nodes.title: L1 full-pullback divisibility/Johnson closure
nodes.statement: On an official dyadic row with k>1 and source petal ell=sigma+1, fix a nontrivial dyadic s|n and s|ell whose monic degree-s fibers partition the domain. A fully fiberwise exact support has size divisible by s, while the source threshold a*=k+ell-1 is not; the class starts at h0=ceil(a*/s) quotient agreements. With b=n/s, K0=ceil(k/s), and d=K0-1, a direct pairwise-intersection argument bounds every fixed-map list by floor(b(h0-d)/(h0^2-bd))<=b^2 whenever h0^2>bd. For s<=k this gate is exactly (k+ell)^2>(k-s)n; for s>k it is automatic. Combining with the tame map census pays all tame fixed-source maps in this full-partition fully fiberwise Johnson sector by at most n b^2<=n^3. This theorem alone leaves the full-partition sub-Johnson, partial-fiber, sparse-coverage, wild, unanchored, and arbitrary-locator branches; the later full-domain intrinsic-rigidity theorem routes the first of those to the exact-periodic owner.

nodes.title: L1 full-domain pullback intrinsic rigidity
nodes.statement: Let H=alpha*mu_n lie in a finite field, let s|n, and let P be monic of degree s. If complete s-point level fibers of P partition all of H, then multiplying their locators gives X^n-alpha^n=F(P). Hence K(X^n) is contained in K(P) inside the cyclic Galois extension K(X)/K(X^n). The unique order-s subgroup fixes K(X^s), so K(P)=K(X^s); polynomial behavior at infinity and monicity force P=X^s+c. Thus every full-domain pullback partition is the intrinsic mu_s quotient, and every fully fiberwise exact support is owned by pma_exact_periodic_owner. There is no non-intrinsic full-domain residual, including the former sub-Johnson sector. General pullback escape requires incomplete domain fibers, partial-fiber agreement, or failure to carry a whole fixed-source petal.

nodes.title: L1 partial-pullback Johnson router
nodes.statement: For one monic degree-s map, let B be its b complete domain-fiber labels, let k_j=ceil((k-j)/s), and let kappa=sum_j max(0,k_j-b). For a listed codeword, let z count agreement points not contained in a fully agreed complete fiber. Then |Agr|=s|E|+z exactly. Under z<=Z, the quotient tuple agrees on at least h_Z=ceil((k+ell-1-Z)/s) labels. If h_Z^2>b(ceil(k/s)-1), a direct interleaved Johnson count bounds the class by q^kappa b^2 per map. Under a tame whole-petal anchor, fixed kappa<=K, and q<=n^gamma, all map classes cost at most n^(3+gamma K). This theorem leaves the nonpositive gate, kernel, wild maps, and missing anchors; the later coverage/kernel tradeoff proves kappa<=max(0,z-ell+1), absorbing the kernel into growing partial loss. The exact F_17^* affine-quadratic witness has z=5, kappa=0, and lies on the nonpositive side.

nodes.title: L1 pullback coverage/kernel tradeoff
nodes.statement: For a monic degree-s pullback with b complete domain fibers, the general-descent component dimensions k_j satisfy sum_j max(0,k_j-b)=max(0,k-sb). Thus the evaluation-kernel exponent kappa is exactly the shortfall between code dimension k and complete-fiber coverage sb. For every listed word at threshold k+ell-1, partial agreement loss z satisfies z>=max(0,k+ell-1-sb), hence kappa<=max(0,z-ell+1). In particular z<=ell-1 forces kappa=0, and z<=ell-1+K forces kappa<=K. Composed with the partial-pullback Johnson router and q<=n^gamma, every strict-gate tame anchored box with that loss cap costs at most n^(3+gamma K). Unbounded kappa is not an independent escape; it requires growing partial-loss excess. The nonpositive gate, wild or unanchored maps, and growing loss remain.

nodes.title: L1 raw support-ledger exponential route fence
nodes.statement: On the formal official-rate-half family n=2^j, k=n/2, ell=n/j, M=j/2, b=1 with j a power of two at least 16, the balanced support profile touching every petal in ell/2 points satisfies the source, list-threshold, saturation-width, and per-petal-cap arithmetic. Nevertheless the raw root-pinning right-hand side is at least 2^(n/4), while even one exact-pattern background-anchor allowance is at least q^(n/8). Hence raw support-profile summation or independent per-pattern union bounds cannot close L1; an algebraic feasibility theorem, collective cross-pattern injection, or globally paid quotient/Forney classification is necessary. No realizability or RS-list lower bound is claimed.

nodes.title: L1 exact-shell prefix/Hankel bridge
nodes.statement: For every received word U and every exact agreement size a>k, the exact first-match zero shell E_a(U) of the a-support interpolation-prefix map is in bijection with degree-below-k codewords having exact agreement a, and #ImgFib_U(s)=sum_(a>=s)#E_a(U). In any admissible sunflower source, fixing missed core D and noncore support X identifies the global depth-(a-k) prefix zero condition unitriangularly with the existing saturated Hankel condition T_(X,d)(L_D)=0, including both exactness guards. Thus L1 may close either by row-sharp Q for primitive received-word exact shells with quotient shells paid separately, or by direct fixed-source Hankel aggregation. Toy power-sum Q and the special F2 Myerson statement do not transfer without an explicit chart theorem.

nodes.title: L1 received-word barycentric Q scope fence
nodes.statement: For every a-support A and received word U, vanishing of the top w=a-k coefficients of I_A(U) is equivalent to the w barycentric moments sum_(x in A) U(x)x^j/L_A'(x)=0. These weights depend on the complete moving support. A depth-one F_7 witness has two supports with the same locator prefix and different received-word prefixes, and a nonzero four-support exchange defect excludes a literal affine fixed-column representation. Therefore upstream locator-prefix row-sharp Q does not directly apply to L1 exact shells; the global route requires a new received-word barycentric prefix-flatness theorem or an explicit map-and-owner transport. This does not exclude nonlinear or chart-specific transport.

nodes.title: L1 fixed-syndrome multiprefix source and route cut
nodes.statement: For a monic degree-c polynomial fold with complete c-point fibers, fixing h partial fibers and r partial points and bucketing f full-fiber labels by t leading quotient coefficients gives one exact-boundary received word with at least ceil(binomial(|Q|-h,f)/|B|^t) codewords whenever 0<K<=A<=|D|, A=r+cf, and r+c(f-t-1)<K. Under upstream's printed complete-fold contract, the M31 (u,v)=(1,1) specialization has exact floor 1693898, refuting a universal per-profile cap 29. Independently, an F_17^* same-remainder pair has distinct actual agreement- and error-locator prefixes in both orientations. Hence an arbitrary-word fixed-syndrome count is a sum over attained prefixes; a maximum-prefix-fiber bound alone is insufficient without target coalescing/payment and first-match ownership. No L1 upper payment, M31 closure, or prize endpoint is asserted.

nodes.title: L1 exact-shell complement Toeplitz normal form
nodes.statement: On a multiplicative-coset domain with locator Z^n-beta, let A have size a, w=a-k, and let M be the degree-(n-a) locator of its complement. The barycentric exact-shell moment sum_(x in A)U(x)x^j/L_A'(x) equals [Z^(n-j-1)]U(Z)M(Z). Hence deg I_A(U)<k iff UM has a length-w coefficient gap in degrees n-w through n-1. This fixed Toeplitz map is invariant under adding any degree-below-k codeword to U. Exact agreement shells are in bijection with monic complement divisors M of Z^n-beta in the Toeplitz zero section whose cofactor is coprime to M. The remaining global theorem is primitive Toeplitz split-divisor flatness or a paid transport to upstream prefix-affine divisor Q; no flatness is asserted here.

nodes.title: L1 exact-shell fixed-cofactor prefix transport
nodes.statement: After translating a received word by a degree-below-k codeword, let h be its degree. An exact agreement shell of size a>k is empty for a>h; otherwise its error cofactor Q in U-P=L_A Q has forced degree e=h-a and leading coefficient lc(U). For fixed Q, triangular multiplication determines the first min(a,a-k+e) nonleading coefficients of L_A, so the cell lies in one locator-prefix fiber. There are q^e possible Q. At e=0 the exact shell is exactly one depth-(a-k) locator-prefix fiber and exactness is automatic. The q^e union is an exact structural statement, not a budget verdict: for e<k its ambient cancellation and image-collapse penalty are supplied by l1_cofactor_depth_budget_cancellation, and its distinct targets form the graph proved by l1_cofactor_prefix_pade_graph_normal_form. No locator-Q bound, depth-uniform transport, graph-intersection theorem, or e>=k payment is asserted.

nodes.title: L1 cofactor-depth budget cancellation and sparse-image fence
nodes.statement: For an exact shell with w=a-k and forced cofactor degree 0<=e<k, fixed-cofactor transport gives |E_a(U)|<=q^e B_(a,w+e), where B is the largest full split-locator prefix fiber. Hence an ambient-normalized depth-(w+e) bound cancels q^e exactly and returns the natural depth-w scale. Under image normalization the exact residual factor is q^(w+e)/L_(a,w+e), and integer ceilings contribute less than q^e. At the deployed rows the deeper ambient mean first becomes subunit, and the raw possible-cofactor union first exceeds the row budget, at e=2 for KoalaBear and e=1 for Mersenne-31. This is a route fence, not a counterexample: the follow-on Pade normal form identifies the collective target as a graph, while depth-uniform Q, divisor/graph transversality, and e>=k remain open.

nodes.title: L1 cofactor-prefix Pade graph normal form
nodes.statement: For an exact shell with w=a-k, forced cofactor degree 0<=e<k, and d=w+e, reverse the high coefficients. The product equations are Qhat(T)Lhat(T)=Uhat(T) mod T^(d+1). As Qhat ranges over its q^e choices with fixed nonzero constant term, Lhat=Uhat/Qhat gives a q^e-point codimension-w polynomial graph in depth-d locator-prefix space; projection to the first e locator coefficients is bijective and recovers Qhat by Uhat/Lhat mod T^(e+1). Exact shell members are exactly the split degree-a locators whose prefixes meet this graph and whose recovered cofactors satisfy the complement gcd guard. The graph has ambient density q^(-w). No divisor/graph transversality, quotient payment, or e>=k bound is asserted.

nodes.title: L1 full-locator Pade section for all cofactor degrees
nodes.statement: For every exact shell degree, put w=a-k, e=deg(U)-a, and d=e+w with no restriction on e. For a full reversed monic locator Lhat, deg(U-LQ)<k is equivalent to the w quotient coefficients [T^(e+1..e+w)] Uhat/Lhat vanishing; the first e+1 quotient coefficients recover Q. Exact shells are exactly the split locators in this full-locator Pade section whose recovered cofactors satisfy the complement gcd guard. If e<k, the section is the prefix Pade graph times F^(k-e) and has exactly q^k ambient locator points. If e>=k, the same section remains exact as the reciprocal continues past locator degree a, but no cardinality, codimension, transversality, or row-sharp bound is asserted.

nodes.title: L1 Pade-remainder Jacobian and tangent dichotomy
nodes.statement: For monic degree-a locator L with Euclidean division U=LQ+P, the differential of the remainder map in direction D is -(QD mod L). If gcd(L,Q)=1, multiplication by Q is an automorphism of F[Z]/(L), so the full remainder Jacobian has rank a and the w=a-k high-remainder Pade equations have rank exactly w. Thus the section is a smooth local complete intersection of codimension w there, and every rank-deficient point lies on Res(L,Q)=0. For exact split locators the complement guard gives the canonical partition gcd(Q,Omega)=1 versus tangent D=gcd(L,Q)!=1 with all D-roots inside the agreement support. An exact F_17 tangent witness has projected rank 2<3. No split-point bound or tangent payment is asserted.

nodes.title: L1 tangent Hasse root-pinning census
nodes.statement: For an exact shell member U-P=LQ on a squarefree split domain, the canonical tangent owner is T=gcd(L,Q). Fixing a degree-r domain divisor D|L gives D|Q iff D^2|U-P, equivalently P and its first Hasse derivative match U at every D-root. This confluent evaluation map on degree-below-k codewords has rank min(k,2r), so each fixed exact owner supports at most q^max(k-2r,0) members and the degree-r tangent stratum has size at most binom(n,r)q^max(k-2r,0), without support-subset overcount. Multiplication by Q modulo L has rank a-r, so the w=a-k Pade Jacobian has corank at most min(w,r). The raw binomial sum is not asserted to be row-sharp.

nodes.title: L1 tangent confluent-packet packing
nodes.statement: For an exact shell of size a, let r_P=deg gcd(L_P,Q_P) be each member's tangent degree. Confluent packets give sum_{P:r_P>=j} binom(r_P,j)binom(a-j,k-2j)<=binom(n,j)binom(n-j,k-2j). In the balanced band, with omega=n-a and s=n-2a+k, the weighted intersection law gives the companion bound sum_{P:r_P>=j}binom(r_P,j)binom(omega,s-j)<=binom(n,j)binom(n-j,s-j). Its j=0 case is complement packing and consecutive tail-ceiling ratio is (w+j+1)/(r0-j), so positive j helps exactly above r0>w+1. These exact field-independent families avoid summing formal gcd owners but can remain exponential; no primitive flatness is asserted.

nodes.title: L1 tangent double-root descent to a primitive shell
nodes.statement: Fix an exact tangent owner D=gcd(L,Q) of degree r in U-P=LQ. If 2r<=k, let P_D=U mod D^2 and W_D=(U-P_D)/D^2. Then P=P_D+D^2R bijects the exact-D tangent stratum with the primitive exact shell of W_D on the punctured domain H\roots(D), with parameters (n-r,k-2r,a-r,e-r,w+r); exact ownership plus the complement guard is exactly gcd(Q_0,Omega/D)=1 in the reduced shell. If 2r>k, one D supports at most one codeword. The punctured domain need not remain smooth and no sum over D is asserted.

nodes.title: L1 Pade split-section/support-moment inversion
nodes.statement: For any evaluation set and m>=k, the number C_m(U) of m-subsets on which U has a degree-below-k interpolant equals the split-point count of the unguarded full-locator Pade section and equals sum_{a>=m} binom(a,m)Z_a(U), where Z_a counts codewords with complete agreement size a. The exact-shell gcd guard selects Z_m, and finite binomial inversion gives Z_a=sum_{m>=a}(-1)^(m-a)binom(m,a)C_m. Thus upstream's shifted-lattice/split-pencil support census is exactly the unguarded Pade split count and directly upper-bounds the exact shell. Primitive-owner and finite base-field budget conventions are not identified by this transform.

nodes.title: L1 exact-shell balanced shifted-lattice reduction
nodes.statement: At agreement m>k with w=m-k, omega=n-m, and 2m<=n+k-1, form the shifted interpolation module M_U={(W,N):N=W Uhat mod Omega}. A reduced basis has degrees d1+d2=n-k+1. If d1<=w, the unguarded support census is empty or all m-subsets of one unique codeword's exact agreement set of size n-d1>=m+1, so the complete-agreement level-m shell is empty. Hence every nonempty exact shell has w+1<=d1<=d2<=omega and lies uniquely in the balanced pencil (W,N)=A g1+B g2 with coefficient-space dimension omega-w+1, W a monic degree-omega divisor of Omega, and exactness guard gcd(Q,W)=1. No balanced-pencil count or finite base-field budget is proved.

nodes.title: L1 deep exact-shell Johnson closure
nodes.statement: For any Reed-Solomon code and agreement m with m^2>n(k-1), the ordinary list size is at most floor(n(m-k+1)/(m^2-n(k-1))). At m_J=floor((n+k-1)/2)+1 the denominator is positive, so the entire list is at most n^2. Every exact shell with 2m>n+k-1 lies in that one threshold list; hence all deep exact shells together cost at most n^2, or 2^88 over the full prize box n<=2^44. This is a polynomial L1 payment, not an exact finite-reserve claim. The balanced band is not counted.

nodes.title: L1 band complement-dimension packing
nodes.statement: For an exact level-m shell in 2m<=n+k-1, put omega=n-m, w=m-k, and s=omega-w=n-2m+k>=1. The balanced coefficient space has projective dimension s. Distinct codewords have agreement intersection at most k-1, so their omega-element complement root sets intersect in at most s-1 points. Hence Z_m(U)<=floor(binom(n,s)/binom(omega,s)). At linear complement density this is exp(O(s)), paying fixed s and reserve-sublinear s, but it can be exponential at the deployed linear-s frontier.

nodes.title: L1 interior BC floor routes to higher-shell Q
nodes.statement: For a strict-interior profile d1>=m-k+2, put m'=k-1+d1>m. Every codeword in Paper D's level-m' identity-prefix floor agrees completely on exactly m' points. Its binom(m',m) level-m support witnesses have positive agreement cofactor dividing the complement locator, so all fail the exact-shell gcd guard. Binomial inversion cancels their contribution to Z_m, while each codeword is retained once in Z_m'. Since d1=(m'-k)+1, that true shell is boundary Q. Thus the named base-field support floor is higher-shell Q mass, not an unavoidable L1 exact-interior floor; other guarded interior members remain open.

nodes.title: L1 polynomial-led interior cells are deeper-Q curves
nodes.statement: Let H subset B, m>k, w=m-k, and 1<=e<=k. For a base-field polynomial-led word U monic of degree m+e, every exact level-m codeword has U-P=L_T R_s, where the first e locator coefficients s determine the monic degree-e cofactor triangularly and the next w locator coefficients recursively. Hence Z_m(U) is exactly the disjoint sum over s in B^e of depth-(w+e) locator-prefix fibers along an injective curve theta_z, retaining gcd(R_s,Omega/L_T)=1 in each slice. Ambient means cancel the B^e slice count, but a discrete max-fiber bound leaves a B^e additive term. Nonconstant minimal vectors and e>k remain open.

nodes.title: L1 split-pencil content is exact-shell excess
nodes.statement: For any basis g1,g2 of the received-word interpolation module, let (W,N)=A g1+B g2 have W a monic squarefree complement locator of degree n-m and N=Wc with deg c<k. The monic coefficient content G=gcd(A,B) is basis invariant, divides W, and satisfies Agr_H(U,c)=(H\Z(W)) disjoint union Z(G), so agr(U,c)=m+deg G. Thus level-m exactness is equivalent to gcd(A,B)=1, while division by G uniquely sends every nonprimitive raw member to the same codeword at its true higher shell. The exact BC residual is precisely the primitive coprime coefficient-pair split-pencil census; no bound on that census is asserted.

nodes.title: L1 boundary shifted-lattice affine Q cell
nodes.statement: In the balanced shifted-lattice band, the boundary profile d1=w+1,d2=omega has coordinates (W,N)=A g1+B g2 with deg(A)<=omega-w-1 and scalar B. Projectively, B=0 is one fixed-codeword ray from which the exact guard retains at most one member; B!=0 is the unique guarded affine cell g2+A g1. When W1=1 this is exactly a locator-Q fiber with the top w+1 coefficients prescribed. For nonconstant W1 it remains a quotient/residue affine Q cell. Thus the boundary belongs to Q and the interior BC census starts at d1>=w+2; no Q or BC bound is proved.

nodes.title: L1 boundary-Q planted-root descent
nodes.statement: For an exact member P in a boundary affine-Q cell, the basis determinant gives W1 P-N1=c_P L, where L is its complete agreement locator. With D=gcd(W1,Omega), the module congruence gives D|N1, every D-root is a planted agreement, and D|L. Dividing by D leaves a root-free projective rational-Q cell on H\roots(D). If r=deg D>=k there is at most one member; if r<k, candidates are uniquely P=P_S+D R with deg R<k-r, while the split locator degree falls from m to m-r, preserving surplus w. No smoothness or transport to standard locator Q is proved.

nodes.title: L1 root-free rational-Q projective packing
nodes.statement: After the boundary planted-root descent with r<k, put j=m-r, d=k-r, G=Wbar1 P_S-Nbar1, and V=span(G,W1 F[X]_<d). If the exact cell is nonempty, V has dimension d+1, is gcd-trivial on the punctured domain, and its full projective split-locator intersection is exactly the boundary cell: the infinity hyperplane contains no split locator. Distinct degree-j locator root sets intersect in at most d-1 points, so the cell has size at most floor(binom(n-r,d)/binom(m-r,d)). At linear locator density this is exp(O(d)), paying fixed d and d=o(n) at the corresponding asymptotic reserve scale, but it is not row-sharp for d=Theta(n).

nodes.title: L1 growing-cofactor decorated shift-pair compiler
nodes.statement: Two distinct members of one exact shell compile bijectively to an ordered record Omega=GABN with equal-degree disjoint split tails A,B, degree-e cofactors Q1,Q2, cross-coprimality from exactness, and nonzero residual R=AQ1-BQ2 of degree at most deg(A)-w-1; the ordered record count is exactly Z_a(U)(Z_a(U)-1). At scalar cofactor this is exactly the locator-Q shift-pair/second-moment ledger. For cofactor-primitive records gcd(Q1,Q2)=1 and e<=w, a fixed ordered pair (A,B) supports at most one cofactor decoration. A nonconstant common cofactor divides R and is coprime to ABN, so its domain roots lie in the common agreement core G. The support-pair census, common-cofactor payment, and e>w range remain open.

nodes.title: L1 decorated shift-pair gcd descent and sharpness
nodes.statement: For a decorated record AQ1-BQ2=R, let D=gcd(Q1,Q2) have degree c. Dividing by D gives a primitive record with reduced cofactor degree e-c and increased effective cancellation depth w+c; primitive uniqueness applies whenever e<=w+2c. The common gcd divides R, is coprime to ABN, and all its domain roots lie in the common agreement core G. An explicit F_13 family at w=1,e=2 gives ten primitive cross-coprime decorations of one ordered split pair, each realized by an exact shell pair for a corresponding received word. Thus after gcd descent the e'>w' branch must retain its received-word/Toeplitz owner; the family is not a fixed-word multiplicity or an L1 counterexample.

nodes.title: Micro-lemma: pin the pair-ledger exponent (min(s,t) vs min(s,t-1))
nodes.statement: For two size-(k+t) supports at exchange distance s, the exact pair codimension is t+min(s,t). Thus q^(-min(s,t)) is the conditional second-event cost, while min(s,t-1) is the anchored/projective convention. This is an exponent dictionary, not a proof of averaged slope de-correlation.
nodes.attack_surface: recompute the toy pair-ledger at both exponents vs the exact counts
nodes.falsifier: the toy ledger matching neither exponent
nodes.notes: PROVED exact linear algebra: codim=t+min(s,t). Evidence-only for averaged_xr after canonical false-green correction 3cca68b7.

nodes.title: THE MISSING LEMMA (found by cross-audit): rich-line exhaustiveness at near-k subcores
nodes.statement: Every (t+1)-rich line through a near-k subcore lies in {tangent pencil, quotient-with-tails, dihedral, affine-net} — no fifth class — and the post-strip residue is uniformly capped. The honest open content behind p1's cap; currently supported only by E33 evidence (<= 5 at toys) and the F_193 net cases.

Pro 14-for-14.

nodes.title: bounded coeff norm gate
nodes.statement: For bounded integer coefficients |c_a| <= C and omega of 2-power order M in F_p: P_c(omega) = 0 forces the cyclotomic/coset case (c_a = c_{a+M/2}, counted exactly) OR p | Res(X^{M/2}+1, Q_c) — the explicit cleared norm. Tower sections contain no opposite pairs, so every nonzero tower skew is norm-gated at every imposed odd exponent simultaneously. No bounded-coefficient escape. nodes.title: E22 two-class exhaustion for worst-word challengers
nodes.statement: At the relevant low-slack crossing radii, every non-planted list word for the planted sunflower receiver lies in the structured E15 challenger class: mixed-petal or full-petal. Equivalently, after planted words are removed, there is no one-petal-only or background/core-only third challenger class. The proof uses root-count localization and the ratio-flat obstruction: a third-class word would need to replace r core roots by background roots with r < ell, but constancy on an ell-point petal would force a degree-r polynomial to vanish on ell distinct points, so the replacement is empty and the word is planted.

nodes.falsifier: an exhaustive cell with unclassified > 0, or an explicit low-slack word family outside planted plus mixed/full-petal classes

nodes.title: E22 dyadic local-to-common saturation

nodes.attack_surface: dyadic quotient moduli form a divisibility chain, so larger-modulus fibers refine into fibers of the minimum local modulus
nodes.falsifier: dyadic quotient moduli M_*<M_i where a full M_i-fiber is not a union of full M_*-fibers

nodes.title: E22 quotient-fiber locator saturation
nodes.statement: In the multiplicative subgroup domain, for any divisor M of the domain size and any quotient value z in the image of x -> x^M, divisibility by the fiber locator X^M-z is equivalent to containing the entire fiber {x: x^M=z}. Products of distinct such factors are therefore exactly local unions of full quotient fibers.

nodes.falsifier: a quotient value z whose fiber locator is not X^M-z, or a squarefree support locator divisible by X^M-z without containing the full fiber

Part 2 (the SPAN ESTIMATE: min_j 2^j(2 span_j + 2) <= C sqrt(n), measured C <= 3.2 at six exhaustive scales) = the Dirichlet-with-parity argument, scoped separately. Eleventh satellite; the campaign's first fully-proved root-count theorem at the mid-band. || PART 2-WEAK PROVED (2026-07-10 cycle 33, digest F2_TOWER_P2WEAK_PASS): the span estimate via Dirichlet-with-parity-descent — pigeonhole over k <= Q^2 gives an even difference 2^a delta'; 2-adic valuation descends the smallness to tower level a with cost 2^a <= Q^2; at Q ~ n^{1/3}: THE COMPLETE THEOREM: Z <= 2n/Q + 2Q^2 + 2 <= 4 n^{2/3} + O(n^{1/3}) UNCONDITIONALLY for every non-collapsed trinomial on mu_{2^s}, any odd characteristic. Verified: proved bound dominates the measured worst at six scales (ratio 4.2-5.0 n^{2/3}); pigeonhole certificates exist for every pair at two exhaustive scales. OFFICIAL: 4n^{2/3} = 2^{28.7} << t = 2^36 — nine bits of room; the sqrt-n refinement is optional. The campaign's first COMPLETE unconditional root-count theorem.

F2 s-SPARSE TOWER EXTENSION (2026-07-10, campaign cycle 34; digest F2_SSPARSE_EXTENSION_PASS, 2574 random sets, 3 scales x 3 sparsities, zero violations): for any s-sparse g on mu_{2^s0} with non-collapsed exponent set: Z(g) <= M(g) + min_j 2^j (2 span_j(E) + s - 1), where M(g) = the full-coset root mass (each such coset certifies a binomial factor X^m - c^m | g — STRUCTURED by definition, the coset-union channel) and the residual obeys the tower. Span estimates: adversarial n^{1-1/s} (Dirichlet + parity descent, as Part 2-weak); APPLICATION-SHAPED (AP + window) ~ C sqrt(n) via AP-normalization + two-form Dirichlet (calibrated ~12 sqrt n, log #40). Proof chain (each link proved + machine-verified): full-ladder dictionary -> edge shape lemma (residual < 2^28 < p = 2^31) -> residual determination (unit-triangular, no p-slots below rho) -> r_B = trunc(B^{-1}) = truncated complement locator (product identity) -> SEMIGROUP SUPPORT (B^{-1} of a 2-power coset-union core is supported on multiples of 2^{e_min}; verified exact on 180 random cores) -> residual roots pull back to FULL mu_{2^{e_min}}-cosets -> contradiction with core maximality unless residual empty -> S = maximal coset union. nodes.statement: At every official prize-max row and depth where the consumer's banked generated-field guard |B0|^t>=2^n invokes F2, prove that non-coset-union F2 extras plus trade families are at most n^3=2^123. The July Myerson close and the all-row bounded-class reduction are invalid. The plus generating branch reduces to explicit GRS kernels and the minus generating branch to one coupled negacyclic kernel. Fixed-depth ambient invariance identifies extension-row objects with generated-field objects, but does not transport a depth calibrated using the ambient q. The proved guard/depth reconciliation shows that the full-subset balance (C) selects exactly the five signed generating types, while an exact-slice (T*) depth fails the F2 guard on every type and must use a different route unless the guard is explicitly replaced. Under (C), the working finite mass terminal is Z(L)<=1+n^3; its proof, PP5.0 normalization, and any coset-sensitive Frobenius step remain open. No consumer status is promoted.

F2 L-FUNCTION DIAGONALIZATION (2026-07-10, campaign cycle 79; digest F2_LFUNC_DIAGONALIZATION_PASS): the summit's deviation field diagonalizes EXACTLY in Dirichlet L-values at s=1. For odd prime p and G <= (Z/p)^x of index m with |G| = f even, the field S(t) = sum_{g in G} log|1+zeta_p^{tg}| satisfies, POINTWISE FOR EVERY t: S(t) = (fp/(p-1)) * sum over the m-1 nontrivial quotient characters chi of (1-chi(2)) * (L(1,chi)/tau(chi)) * chi(t). Proof: (i) multiplicative Fourier + orthogonality kills all characters nontrivial on G; (ii) 1+x=(1-x^2)/(1-x) factors each coefficient as (chi(2)-1)*a_chi(log|1-zeta^s|); (iii) the classical even-character evaluation sum_a conj(chi)(a) log|1-zeta^a| = -p L(1,chi)/tau(chi) (Washington, Cyclotomic Fields, Thm 4.9 shape; numerically confirmed against independent partial-sum L(1,chi) at p=97,257, all quotient characters, err < 1e-6). COROLLARIES: (a) second moment sum_t S(t)^2 = (f^2 p/(p-1)) sum_chi |1-chi(2)|^2 |L(1,chi)|^2 — the summit's energy IS a mean-square of L(1,chi) over the quotient character group (supersedes the log #89 Dedekind autocorrelation reduction by full diagonalization); (b) DOUBLING VANISHING: 2 in G => S == 0 identically (2G=G, the two ell-sums cancel; subsumes the index-2 vanishing for p = +-1 mod 8 and explains every accidentally-flat probe row, e.g. (257, m=4)); (c) with L(1,chi) = O(log p) the diagonalization re-derives the ETK-scale bound, so growing-order Myerson is EXACTLY the statement that the L-value-weighted character sum sum_chi (1-chi(2))(L(1,chi)/tau(chi))chi(t) exhibits square-root cancellation in m uniformly in t — a STANDARD-FORM object of analytic number theory (character sums with L-value weights; Chowla/class-number circle). Verified: pointwise reconstruction, factorization, second moment at (97,m=3),(257,m=4),(7681,m=15) to 1e-10; doubling rows (7,<2>),(73,<2>) flat to 3e-15. Verifier: background/nodes/u2c_giant_tnull_dichotomy/notes/f2_lfunc_diagonalization_check.py. Sixteenth satellite; the summit's interior is now a NAMED ANT OBJECT.

F2 UNCONDITIONAL SECOND-MOMENT BUDGET (2026-07-10, campaign cycle 80; digest F2_SECOND_MOMENT_BUDGET_PASS): first unconditional control of the summit's deviation field at ALL growing orders. From the L-function diagonalization (satellite f2_lfunc_diagonalization): (i) S is constant on cosets of G — the field has only m distinct values; (ii) sum_t S(t)^2 = (f^2 p/(p-1)) sum_{chi != 1} |1-chi(2)|^2 |L(1,chi)|^2 exactly; (iii) RMS_t S <= 2 sqrt(f) max|L(1,chi)| — with the classical even-character bound L(1,chi) <= (1/2)log p + O(1) (explicit Louboutin-type constants), RMS <= ~sqrt(f) log p UNCONDITIONALLY; (iv) EFFECTIVE INDEX: characters trivial on <G,2> contribute zero, so the field descends to the quotient mod the image of 2 (effective dimension m - m/ord_quotient(2); Fermat-prime rows p=65537 are fully degenerate at m=16,256 — found in the wild by the doubling law); (v) Chebyshev tail #{t: |S|>=A} <= 4 f^2 (m-1) M^2/A^2. MEASURED across (97,3)...(786433,768), all pre-registered reads favorable: effective L-constant RMS/sqrt(f) = 1.0-1.6 FLAT over three decades (quotient characters behave like average characters — sum |L(1,chi)|^2 ~ const*m, the classical L(1,chi) second-moment scale); max/RMS grows like sqrt(2 log m) (3.04 at m=768 vs Gaussian 3.65 vs adversarial sqrt(m)=27.7) — the field is GAUSSIAN-LIKE, exactly the square-root-cancellation shape the summit asserts; P(|S|>10 nats) = 0.8-1.0 at f >= 512 — QUANTITATIVE re-confirmation that no pointwise or exceptional-shift consumer route exists (the per-condition budget is exceeded on most shifts once f > ~100; the saving must be signed cancellation in the aggregate over conditions, consistent with no-gos 2 and 9). Verifier: background/nodes/u2c_giant_tnull_dichotomy/notes/f2_second_moment_budget_check.py. Seventeenth satellite; the summit now has an unconditional moment theory.

F2 ANNEALED/PHASE SPLIT (2026-07-10, campaign cycle 81; digest F2_ANNEALED_PHASE_SPLIT_PASS): the consumer contract's Fourier anatomy, pinned. (I) CENSUS-FOURIER IDENTITY (orthogonality, exact; verified integer-exact against the DP census at (97,32,j=2), all b): N_b^(j) = (1/q^j) sum_{c in F_q^j} [z^b] prod_{x in mu_n}(1 + z psi(c.(x,..,x^j))). The period product splits into MODULUS field S_c = sum_x log|1+psi(c.xbar)| (= the satellites-16/17 field) and PHASE field Phi_c. (II) ANNEALED DEATH CONSTANT: E_c[exp(S_c)] = (4/pi)^{n(1+o(1))} under phase equidistribution (E_theta|1+e(i theta)| = 4/pi, one line); at official depth q^t = 2^{2.15e12} >> exp(0.411 n) the Gaussian tail is fully available, so ANY absolute/triangle-inequality route (annealed, max, or L-value moments of |S|) misses the n^3 budget by >= n log2(4/pi) ~ 0.3485 n ~ 3.8e11 bits — the required signed recovery is the ENTIRE annealed mass; no bound on |S| alone can close the contract. Measured at 6 rows: rates 0.10-0.26 nats/root, every deviation from the ideal explained and checked (CATCH #20: finite-frequency-population cap — q^j points cannot realize the tail S ~ 0.822n unless j log q > 0.411 n; sampled estimators are tail-blind/biased-low, the sample-max-dominated formula (maxS - log N)/n reproduced every low rate to 0.001; the exact-population j=3 rate 0.2569 slightly EXCEEDS the discrete envelope 0.2416 — mild positive dependence — the death constant is a FLOOR). (III) PHASE FIELD = GENERALIZED DEDEKIND SUM (proved per-factor: arg(1+e(i theta)) = theta/2, psi never -1 at odd q): Phi_c = pi * sum_{x in mu_n} ((c.xbar/q)) with ((.)) the centered sawtooth — verified to 5e-13 at all rows. REDIRECT (the split's consequence for the summit lane): the census's needed cancellation is the mod-2pi oscillation of Phi_c — a SAWTOOTH/DEDEKIND SUM OVER THE SUBGROUP, the exact classical home of Dedekind reciprocity and Vardi/Conrey distribution theory; the L-function diagonalization governs the modulus component, reciprocity must govern the phase. Verifier: background/nodes/u2c_giant_tnull_dichotomy/notes/f2_annealed_phase_split_modal.py. Eighteenth satellite; the summit's open content now has coordinates: (modulus, phase) = (L-values at 1, Dedekind sawtooth sums).

F2 SIGN QUANTIZATION THEOREM (2026-07-10, campaign cycle 82; digest F2_PHASE_CANCELLATION_PASS): the phase field is PI-QUANTIZED — every census frequency term is a SIGNED REAL. For j < n, Phi_c = pi * sum_{x in mu_n}((c.xbar/q)) is an integer multiple of pi: sum_x (c.xbar mod q) = c.(p_1(mu_n),..,p_j(mu_n)) = 0 mod q because full-group power sums vanish below index n, so the sawtooth sum is an INTEGER (one-paragraph proof; discovered by the Weyl k=2 sums measuring exactly 1.0000 at every row). Hence prod_{x in mu_n}(1+psi(c.xbar)) = eps_c * exp(S_c) with SIGN eps_c = (-1)^{#{x in mu_n : c.xbar mod q > q/2}} — a half-interval count parity, purely combinatorial. COROLLARIES: (a) j=1 phase vanishing for even f (verified exactly); (b) THE SUMMIT REFRAMED: growing-order Myerson at official rows = square-root cancellation of the RADEMACHER-TYPE sign field eps_c weighted by exp(S_c) — the census deviation is q^j N_total - 2^n = sum_{c != 0} eps_c exp(S_c), an identity verified exactly against integer DP censuses at (97,32,j=2), (97,32,j=3), (193,64,j=2) to 6e-15. FIRST ALIGNMENT MEASUREMENT (the falsifier-adjacent number): R/R_pred = measured signed recovery vs random-sign prediction sqrt(sum exp 2S)/sum exp S = 6.53, 7.98, 7.41 at the three exact rows — systematically ~7x above perfect-random but FLAT across rows so far; unweighted sign imbalance |E eps| = 0.002-0.15 (nearly balanced, one notable 0.148 at (193,64)). Pre-registered continuation: if the alignment factor GROWS with scale (more exact rows, higher j), the sign-magnitude correlation is the danger lane — measure before any proof attempt; if it stabilizes O(1), constant-factor alignment is absorbable in the 2^15-per-condition slack. Verifier: background/nodes/u2c_giant_tnull_dichotomy/notes/f2_phase_cancellation_modal.py. Nineteenth satellite; the summit's coordinates sharpen: (modulus, sign) = (L-values/Gaussian field, half-interval parities). CATCH #21 CORRECTION (cycle 83): the sign formula omitted the carry — correctly eps_c = (-1)^{K + U} with K = (sum_x s_x)/q (an integer by the quantization theorem) and U = #{x : s_x > q/2}; the omission was formula-transcription only (the cycle-82 verifier summed exact arguments; theorem and identities stand; corrected formula re-verified integer-exact at 12 rows, digest F2_ALIGNMENT_SCALING_PASS). ALIGNMENT SCALING STUDY (cycle 83, 12 exact rows, populations 12.7k-36.3M): j=2 subfamily FLAT at R/R_pred ~ 7 +- 2 with no growth over 35x population; j=3 inflation (up to 60 at (113,16)) AUTOPSIED as 100% STRUCT DRIFT, not sign alignment — brute-force at (113,16,j=3) over all 2^16 subsets: N_total = 16 = EXACTLY the 16 coset-union blocks, EXTRAS = 0 (that row verifies the F2 dichotomy literally, zero extras; the deviation is the forced struct census, deterministic and positive). METHODOLOGICAL LAW: the falsifier-adjacent number is the STRUCT-SUBTRACTED alignment |q^j(N-struct) - 2^n| / random-sign scale; struct_total = 2^{n/4} at 2-power n for j in {2,3} (unions of scaled mu_M-cosets, M >= 4; confirmed exhaustively at (113,16)). Twisted-orbit invariance of (S, eps) under c_i -> lambda^i c_i proved (one line: it is x -> lambda x) and verified; effective frequency population (q^j-1)/n.

MEASURED at 13 exact 2-power-n rows, frequency populations 12.7k to 44.0M (q = 97..1153, n = 16..64, j = 2,3): ALL rows in one band ratio' = 0.17..11.4, least-squares slope of log(ratio') vs log(population) = -0.067 => STABILIZATION — the alignment factor is a scale-stable O(1) constant ~7, four orders below the 2^15-per-condition slack. One row sub-random (769,64: 0.78). Verified at (p,k) = (7,2), (5,2), (3,4): quantization exact at every frequency, census-Fourier identity integer-exact against F_{p^k} DP censuses (field arithmetic via irreducible-polynomial construction), alignment ratios 8.7/4.0/1.9 in the satellites-19/20 band. Every prime-q campaign measurement is now backed by a proved-and-verified transfer principle to the tower. F2 LADDER TERMINATION (2026-07-10, campaign cycle 86; digest F2_RUNG2_LADDER_PASS, reads corrected by CATCH #22): the alphabet ladder terminates at rung 1 — the summit's sign problem is irreducible. Consequently the imagined telescoping induction (each rung's alignment controlled by the next) is DEAD as a proof lane — no-go #10 for the campaign ledger: the summit's signed content lives irreducibly in the rung-1 sign field eps_c = (-1)^{K+U}, and any proof must engage that combinatorial parity directly (Ehrhart/lattice-parity, Dedekind-integer reciprocity, or a genuinely new mechanism). nodes.title: H3 quotient multiplicities are coefficient-coset block sizes minus one
nodes.statement: For A=(1-H)\{0} and nonidentity t, set u(t)=1/(1-t), v(t)=-t/(1-t), and partition F_p\{0,1} by the HxH coefficient coset (u(t)H,v(t)H). If B is a block and t is in B, then the quotient multiplicity R(t)=#{(c,d) in A^2:d/c=t} equals |B|-1 and is constant on B. Consequently sum_B |B|(|B|-1)=(n-1)(n-2). Proof: coefficient points in a block are (u(t)h,v(t)k) on U+V=1; (h,k)=(1,1) is the unique zero/zero excluded pair, and every other point is exactly one valid shifted quotient representation. nodes.title: H3 non-swap collisions are a directed quotient-line chord moment
nodes.statement: Put C_m={a in A:ma in A}, so |C_m|=R(m). The exact non-swap collision multiplicity Q(t)=P(t)(P(t)-2)+D(t) equals the number of triples (m,a,a') with m!=1, a!=a', a,a' in C_m, and m*a*a'=t. Hence S_ns=sum_{m!=1}sum_{a!=a' in C_m,maa'!=1}R(maa'), while S_ns^rich restricts the inner sum to P(maa')>=19. This is a proved bijection and re-poses C36' as a directed source-line/target-line correlation; it does not assert the open 1200n^2 rich-moment bound. Two complete symbolic fences reject an automatic non-base target in the natural Laurent-monomial ansatz and every direct coordinate-permutation embedding of the six subgroup variables into one classical collinear-triple equation.

nodes.title: Generic MDS residual charts have a field-independent ray bound
nodes.statement: Let an MDS parity-check restriction on U have rank R, |U|=R+d, and let 1<=h<=R, r=R-h. For a syndrome line with no common r-sparse support for both endpoints, if every slope in Z has an r-sparse lift supported in U, then |Z| C(d+h,d) <= C(R+d,d)R. Proof: after the trivial |Z|<=1 case, two supported slopes supply endpoint lifts; the MDS kernel restricts bijectively to every d-set T, and after cancelling T genericity leaves fewer than h persistent zeros, so every sparse slope supplies C(d+h,d) nonpersistent affine-zero charges while each (T,x) receives at most one slope. This is a fixed-chart ray theorem, not an aggregate atlas. Revised upstream PR #1106 records that the merged agreement-weighted transverse-secant theorem strictly dominates this specialization at KoalaBear, paying nullities through ten under per-witness transversality supplied by column-farness.

nodes.title: High-direction-distance residual charts have at most N squared rays
nodes.statement: Let H_U:F^U->F^R have kernel K, put N=|U|, and let d_U(y1) be the minimum weight of a lift of the nonzero syndrome direction y1. If every slope in Z on y0+gamma y1 has a lift of weight at most t in U and (N-t)^2>N(N-d_U(y1)), then |Z|<=floor(N(d_U(y1)-t)/((N-t)^2-N(N-d_U(y1))))<=N^2. Proof: the selected slopes give distinct words of K+<b1> inside one radius-t Hamming ball; agreement-set second moments pay them. Failure of the inequality gives an explicit sparse-direction lift and is the exact complementary branch. This is a fixed-chart theorem and does not aggregate charts.

nodes.title: Dyadic shifted roots are multiplicatively Sidon in characteristic zero
nodes.statement: Let n=2^s and A=(1-mu_n(C))\{0}. Then ab=cd with a,b,c,d in A forces {a,b}={c,d}; every nonidentity quotient fiber also has multiplicity at most one. Proof: the 2-adic cyclotomic valuation first matches the two valuation levels; separating Q(zeta_{2^j}) over Q(zeta_{2^{j-1}}) then gives either the two factors separately or their sum and product. Hence every finite-field non-equal, non-swap product collision lifts to a nonzero cyclotomic integer alpha=(1-x)(1-y)-(1-u)(1-v) killed modulo the row prime, so p divides Norm(alpha) and 0<|Norm(alpha)|<=6^phi(n). It also gives the exact finite split S_ns=sum_{R(t)>0}Q(t)+sum_t Q(t)(R(t)-1), separating one norm-gate accident from the joint double-accident term. This is not a per-prime aggregate bound or a proof of S_ns^rich<=1200n^2.

nodes.title: C36' fifth product-orbit moment compiler
nodes.statement: Let U(t)=(P(t)+D(t))/2 be the number of unordered product representations and M_5^rich=sum_{t!=1,P(t)>=19}binom(U(t),5)R(t). Then X_18<=(2/231)M_5^rich, with sharp compiler equality at (P,D,U)=(22,0,11). Consequently M_5^rich<=(34650/17)n^2 implies the critical target 17X_18<=300n^2. The reduction is proved; the moment estimate is not claimed.

nodes.title: Canonical high-core component-union atlas
nodes.statement: For a generic post-strip pair, graph live slopes by size-k collisions, equivalently by witness error-set unions of size R=n-k. The nonisolated slopes partition into canonical connected components C. A lexicographic spanning-tree selection chooses one witness ray per slope and a component union U_C of size R+d_C. Each slope has an r=n-A supported lift in U_C, genericity is inherited, and GRK gives |Z_C|C(d_C+h,d_C)<=C(R+d_C,d_C)R. Hence the high-core slope count is the exact disjoint sum over C and is at most sum_C floor(C(R+d_C,d_C)R/C(d_C+h,d_C)). This resolves core/chart/slope deduplication but does not bound the component count or excess ledger by 8n^3.

nodes.title: All-LineRay affine-core set-pair bound
nodes.statement: Let P be all distinct transverse sparse error pairs on one nonconstant syndrome line, let s be their affine error rank, and let w be their maximum weight. Zero-mask restriction is injective on the affine core; canonical full-rank zero minors form a nonuniform Bollobas set-pair system. Therefore sum_(gamma,e)1/C(s+wt(e),s)<=1 and |P|<=C(s+w,s)<=C(n,s). Applying the same theorem to any one-per-slope selector gives #slopes<=C(sigma+r,sigma), where sigma is the minimum selector rank and r=n-A. Exact arithmetic at all six XR candidates pays sigma<=3, while sigma=4 fails. Thus both XR predicates are paid whenever a rank-at-most-three selector exists; every selector in the residual has rank at least four.

nodes.title: Support-wise transverse LineRay rank charge
nodes.statement: For a selected LineRay error e_z=u+zv-p_z with zero mask S_z, support-wise nontriviality on that same S_z is equivalent to the pointwise transversality condition {Hu,Hv} not subset H(F^supp(e_z)). Hence the all-LineRay selector inequality applies to the entire support-mismatch population even if the received pair has a joint explanation on another support: #slopes<=C(sigma+n-A,sigma). Exact official-row arithmetic pays sigma<=3 from an 8n^3 half-reserve everywhere and also sigma=4 from P-A2's full combined 16n^3 reserve at RowC rate 1/4. A P-A2 counterexample therefore has minimum selector rank at least 5 there and at least 4 on the other five rows.

nodes.title: High-core collision-line basis ledger

If b_ell counts its independent (s-1)-minors, then sum_ell b_ell<=C(n,s-1), while each line contains at most floor((n-k)/(A-k)) errors. A minimum-basis line with b_*=b puts the whole affine family in a fixed chart of excess at most b+s-2 and self-localizes the line ledger to |P_hi|<=L floor(C(min(n,R+b+s-2),s-1)/b). This closes rank four on RowC 1/4 and prize 1/4,1/8 before the cogirth handoff.

Charging nonpersistent zeros gives |P|C(Delta-r+a-1,a)<=C(N,a)(N-a). nodes.title: C36' rich product fibers are confined below the 6^(n/4) norm threshold

Ten unordered representations forced by P>=19 yield ten odd-conjugate coefficient vectors. At most two are diagonal and at most one contains -1, so at least seven have squared norm at most 3. The seven-vector centroid identity forces a pair at squared distance at most 6. Parseval and AM-GM give a nonzero collision obstruction of norm at most 6^(n/4). Thus X_18=0 for p>6^(n/4), reducing the open C36' range to n^2<=p<=6^(n/4).

nodes.title: C36' same-fiber collision norms factor through one minimal cyclotomic ideal
nodes.statement: Let n=2^s, O=Z[zeta_n], pi=1-zeta_n, and P=(p,zeta_n-g) for a selected degree-one prime above an odd p=1 mod n. For distinct unordered exponent pairs with one common shifted product modulo P, let alpha_i be their lifted shifted-product differences relative to one reference and J=(alpha_i). Dyadic shifted-product Sidonicity makes every alpha_i nonzero. Uniformly, J is contained in (pi)^2 P, so 4p divides N(J), while N(J) divides every principal norm |Norm(alpha_i)|. At the complete boundary rich locus (n,p)=(8192,67657729), each of the two ten-pair fibers has gcd 4p already for its first two collision norms, proving that those two obstructions generate (pi)^2 P exactly. This is ideal-level batching and route evidence only; it does not bound the number or quotient weight of rich fibers.

nodes.title: L1: mixed-petal / diffuse partial-petal amplification is polynomially bounded (large-defect regime)
nodes.statement: At every official row and for every received word U, the mixed-petal or diffuse partial-petal contributors to #ImgFib_U(k+sigma) are polynomially bounded above the corrected reserve, with quotient profiles budgeted. The exact-shell prefix/Hankel bridge gives two honest closure routes: global received-word Toeplitz prefix flatness, or aggregate local first-owner payment in one fixed source. Fixed-cofactor transport writes shell a with forced e=deg(U)-a as at most q^e depth-(a-k+e) locator-prefix fibers, with e=0 exactly one upstream locator-Q atom. Cofactor-depth budget cancellation proves that for e<k this q^e factor cancels under ambient normalization, while image normalization retains q^(a-k+e)/L_(a,a-k+e) and integer rounding loses less than q^e. The cofactor-prefix Pade normal form makes the below-cap targets one graph, and the full-locator Pade section extends the exact split-divisor intersection to every e via the a-k equations [T^(e+1..e+a-k)]Uhat/Lhat=0. Thus the live global task is a tangent first-match payment plus row-sharp split-point concentration on a smooth primitive full-locator Pade section, with depth-uniform Q as its top-prefix edge and decorated support-pair control as its second moment. Canonical cofactor gcd descent removes q^(2e) decoration counting through e<=w+2c; an exact F_13 endpoint family proves the reduced high branch must retain its received-word owner. The raw-ledger fence proves independent support summation exponentially loose. The unpaid local mechanisms are small-scale general-pullback or collective aperiodic-support payment on known tame refinements, wild or unanchored quotient maps, growing signed layout/core-defect/petal polarity, the balanced sub-Johnson strip, and arbitrary petal locators outside one common pencil. Thus closure requires either the global smooth-section/tangent payment or aggregate payment of this narrower internal residual. At the first characteristic checkpoint, all five official next-to-maximal order-zero HNF endpoint chambers are now closed by the m=8 and m=16 reciprocal eliminations; order one, lower value degrees, nonembedded m=4,h=2, and inner lifts remain. nodes.title: DLI ell=2 weight-5 relations reduce to a pair quadratic and two Dickson equations
nodes.statement: Over any official field, every reduced signed weight-5 relation satisfying P(omega)=P(omega^3)=0 admits the following exact normalization. Scale one signed root to 1 and choose two others x,y; with u=x+y, A=xy, v=-1-u, B=u(v-A)/v, the final two roots are exactly the roots of T^2-vT+B. Conversely any guarded pair whose quadratic has two distinct mu_1024 roots reconstructs a relation. With D_0=2, D_1=v, D_m=vD_(m-1)-B D_(m-2), quadratic membership is equivalent to B^1024=1 and D_1024(v,B)=2. This is a two-shape-variable router, not an emptiness theorem.

If the block multiplication matrix L=[M_F M_G] has full rational row rank, its maximal determinantal divisor Delta=[Z[zeta_M]:(F,G)] is divisible by every split-row characteristic supporting that pair.
